headline: New law updates federal programs that prevent and treat child abuse, neglect, and family violence involving Native American children and families.
what_it_does: The law changes a federal grant program for treating abuse of Indian children so that grants are encouraged to pay for culturally appropriate treatment. It renames the regional resource centers as a single National Indian Child Resource and Family Services Center and gives it new duties, including training urban Indian organizations and writing model agreements between tribes and states. It also lets tribes and tribal groups use prevention program money for more purposes, such as day-to-day costs of running child protective services.

who_it_affects.how: They may receive more culturally appropriate services for preventing and treating child abuse, neglect, and family violence.

who_it_affects.group: Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and intertribal consortia
who_it_affects.how: They can use federal child protection program funds for more activities, including operating costs for child protective services, and will receive new technical assistance materials.
They can now get advice, technical help, and training from the national resource center.
They will have model agreements available to help them work with tribes on investigating and prosecuting child abuse and family violence cases.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the summary does not list a separate start date.
